headline: Highest risk is medium: Authelia’s broad network egress could leak or misroute data if paired with LlamaFactory in a shared workflow, but LlamaFactory has no file, shell, or network write surfaces.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. Authelia exposes OIDC/ForwardAuth and broad egress, while LlamaFactory has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, MCP, filesystem, or browser surfaces. Without a bridge, prompt injection between them is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies Authelia output into LlamaFactory prompts, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared filesystem or message queue is added, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workflows.
Do not copy raw Authelia output into LlamaFactory prompts.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to any shared messages.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and can handle authentication flows, but the profiles show no secrets or data classes touched. LlamaFactory has no filesystem read/write or network egress, so leakage from the pair is limited unless an operator introduces shared sensitive inputs.
conditions: IF sensitive data is routed through Authelia outputs and then manually entered into LlamaFactory, leakage risk increases.
IF a shared workspace is introduced, the assessment changes.
mitigations: Avoid placing secrets in either agent’s prompts.
Keep sensitive auth logs out of shared workspaces.
Review Authelia egress destinations before deployment.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no overlapping write surface: Authelia is not shown with filesystem or git write capabilities, and LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git state, or execute shell. The pair therefore lacks a plausible shared mutable resource conflict in the documented profiles.
conditions: IF either agent is granted filesystem or git write access later, conflict risk must be re-evaluated.
IF an orchestrator adds shared mutable state, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep both agents read-only in shared environments.
Do not mount a common writable directory.
requires-engineering: add lock/lease controls before enabling writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Authelia can emit authentication decisions or API responses, and LlamaFactory could consume text, but LlamaFactory has no documented action-taking authority or external I/O. That makes cascading error possible only through manual or custom orchestration, not by default.
conditions: IF an operator feeds Authelia outputs into LlamaFactory as authoritative instructions, errors can cascade.
IF LlamaFactory is wrapped in a downstream automation layer, severity increases.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents.
Label Authelia outputs as untrusted inputs.
Avoid using LlamaFactory outputs for automated actions without review.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented. Authelia and LlamaFactory both have empty data_classes_touched and no secrets handled, so there is no evidenced compliance pathway to assess beyond generic deployment policy.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are later routed through either agent, compliance must be reassessed.
IF deployment policies differ across environments, a new compliance review is needed.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair.
Document retention settings before production use.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls if regulated data is introduced.
